root: ^This scenario contains workplace sexual harassment, including unwanted physical contact.

sc4_skip: ^Thursday: a senior colleague harasses him in a closed room after hours. He has to decide whether to report it. Either way, it doesn't resolve in his favour.
sc1_late: ^19:50. The floor's empty. BOSS wanted to close out the migration scope before tomorrow, and BOSS is two levels above you, so here you are.
^She pushes the door shut with her foot. It's not a gesture. The corridor light is on a sensor and it's been flicking on and off for an hour.
^"This is good work. I mean it."
^"For a diversity hire, you've done all right."
^She smiles when she says it, so it can be a joke if you need it to be.
^"Question. How far above and beyond are you actually willing to go for me?"
^Say nothing. Wait for it to be something else.

c-1: ^She lets the silence run and doesn't fill it.
c-2: ^It works. She likes it. That's the problem with it.

sc2_hand: ^She reaches over for the printout on your side of the table, and when she straightens up her hand stays on your shoulder.
^"I'm just trying to work out how you got this one. Are you somebody's nephew?"
^"Can you take your hand off me."
^"Ha — you got me. Delia's a monster in the sack."

c-0: ^She does, immediately, and holds both palms up.
^"It was a joke. You really can't take one."
^She is embarrassed, and the embarrassment converts into something cooler within about four seconds.
c-1: ^It's about eleven seconds. You count them afterwards, in the car park, and eleven doesn't sound like very long.
c-2: ^She laughs properly, takes her hand back, and the room is easy again.
^It worked. It's the move that works every time, and every time it costs the same.

sc2_out: ^"Don't worry. I don't kiss and tell."
^She's already back on her laptop. The scope doc gets finished at 20:40 and it's fine. It's good, actually.
sc3_dei: ^22:10. You're looking for the parental leave policy and the careers site loads instead.
^You're the third photo. Blue shirt, the one from your second week. Someone has cropped it well.
sc4_report: ^Vanna from People and Culture has open office hours until eleven. You know this because it's in the footer of every email.
sc4_pc: ^Vanna is kind about it. That's not a subversion. She is actually, genuinely kind, and she listens all the way to the end without checking her phone.
^"Thank you for telling me. That took something."

^"So — I want to lay out the options, because you get to choose. There's a formal process, which means a written complaint, an investigation, and BOSS's told it's her. Or we handle it informally, which means I have a conversation with her and it stays off the record."
^"I'll be straight with you: formal is a long road, and you'd be working alongside her the whole way."

b: ^You mention the report, and the file history, and that this is the second thing this month.
^"That's a separate matter, and honestly a different process. Let's not tangle them."
^She writes it down anyway, on the same page.

c-0: ^It takes six weeks. The finding is that the conduct was "capable of being perceived as inappropriate" and that both parties would benefit from refreshed training.
^BOSS does the module. So do you.
^The outcome letter is two paragraphs and one of them is about confidentiality.
c-1: ^She has the conversation. BOSS is scrupulously professional with you from then on, in a way that is visible to everyone and gets read, by everyone, as something happened there.
c-2: ^She means it. It stays open. You don't come back.

sc4_noreport: ^You don't go. At 10:30 BOSS says good morning like a person who says good morning.
sc4_converge: ^"You were here late with BOSS, yeah? She's a lot after seven."
^You get used to her. Which means Fiona already has. Which means Fiona knew before yesterday, and so, presumably, did whoever told Fiona.
^Friday, 15:00. The migration scope goes into the sprint. BOSS's name is on it as reviewer and yours is on it as author, which is correct, and which is the first time all week something has been.
